chunks: And (remember) when We saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who oppressed and afflicted you, slaying your sons and sparing your women. In this was a great trial from your Lord.

key_terms.يَسُومُونَكُمْ: They deal with you / inflict upon you

ai.seo_question: What was the specific nature of Pharaoh's oppression against the Children of Israel as described in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-A'raf is often cited to illustrate the concept of 'balā' al-kabīr' (the great trial), where Pharaoh's systematic destruction of the male lineage was a divine mechanism to preserve the specific lineage of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Imams. The sparing of women is interpreted not merely as mercy but as a strategic preservation of the community's reproductive capacity and spiritual continuity under oppression. This event serves as a paradigm for the suffering of the Ahl al-Bayt and the faithful throughout history, emphasizing that divine deliverance often follows prolonged, targeted tribulation.
